description.value: This study investigated whether tau haplotype modulates cerebral perfusion patterns and clinical phenotypic expression in frontotemporal lobar degeneration and related tauopathies using SPECT imaging.

spans.text: The aim of this study was to determine whether tau genetic variability modulates the brain functional and the clinical phenotypic expression of FTLD.

spans.text: Stringent exclusion criteria were applied, as follows: (i) cerebrovascular disorders, previous stroke, hydrocephalus and intra-cranial mass, documented by MRI; (ii) a history of traumatic brain injury or another neurological disease; (iii) another extrapyramidal syndrome; (iv) significant medical problems; (v) major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or substance use disorder, according to DSM-IV criteria; and (vi) only patients with mild cognitive decline entered the study [Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) ≥18], to avoid confounds in functional data analysis.

cerebral perfusion
The cerebral perfusion assessment in the whole FTLD group revealed a significant frontal involvement as previously described in literature (10).
Cerebral perfusion patterns were analysed according to H1 or H2 tau haplotypes by statistical parametric mapping and principal component analysis.
